system: Blades in the Dark / Forged in the Dark

start_here.one_sentence: Build a d6 action pool, take the highest die, and interpret 6 as full success, 4–5 as success with consequence, and 1–3 as trouble; position and effect frame risk and impact.
required_materials: randomizer or dice appropriate to the system

core_loop.name: Establish fiction
core_loop.details: The facilitator describes the situation, stakes, sensory information, and immediately relevant constraints.

core_loop.name: Declare intent
core_loop.details: A player states what the character wants and how they attempt it. Clarify target, method, tools, and desired effect.

core_loop.name: Decide whether rules engage
core_loop.details: Do not roll when success is certain and uninteresting. Roll or trigger a move only when uncertainty and consequences matter.

core_loop.name: Set stakes and modifiers
core_loop.details: Identify the governing statistic, difficulty, position, effect, opposition, advantage, or cost before randomization whenever possible.

core_loop.name: Resolve
core_loop.details: Build a d6 action pool, take the highest die, and interpret 6 as full success, 4–5 as success with consequence, and 1–3 as trouble; position and effect frame risk and impact.

core_loop.name: Apply outcome
core_loop.details: Change the fiction, resources, clocks, positioning, harm, opportunities, and future choices. Avoid outcomes that leave the situation unchanged.

core_loop.name: Pass spotlight
core_loop.details: Move attention to the character most affected, least recently active, or best positioned to respond.

character_creation: Choose campaign premise, power scale, tone, and allowed sources.
Choose a concept and party function without treating roles as mandatory.
Assign core statistics using the edition-appropriate method.
Select archetype, class, playbook, profession, or point-built capabilities.
Select lineage, ancestry, species, culture, background, or origin only where the system uses them.
Choose skills, abilities, feats, edges, stunts, moves, powers, spells, gear, and relationships.
Calculate derived values and starting resources.
Write motivations, boundaries, connections, and advancement triggers.
Review overlap and gaps with the group, then make final adjustments.
advancement: Mark playbook, attribute, and crew XP from expressed drives and desperate actions; spend XP on action dots, abilities, and crew upgrades.
resources: Stress, trauma, harm, armor, load, coin, stash, heat, wanted level, clocks, claims, crew tier, position, and effect.

principles: check retreat, surrender, morale, or scene end
attack_procedure: select weapon, power, move, or maneuver
build the roll using the system method
compare to defense or outcome band
resolve reactions, resistance, armor, or consequences
record ammunition, stress, slots, durability, or other expenditure

magic_and_special_abilities.applicability: Use only if the campaign and character options permit supernatural, psychic, technological, or extraordinary effects.
casting_procedure: make required roll or impose required defense
apply concentration, sustain, backlash, or consequence rules
design_checks: Does the effect bypass an entire challenge without cost?
Does it duplicate another niche more efficiently?
Does scaling match the campaign tier?

editions_covered_as_index_and_original_s: Blades in the Dark original release
Forged in the Dark SRD lineage
edition_policy.mixing_editions: Do not combine numbers directly. Convert intent, expected success rate, action economy, durability, and resource cadence separately.
edition_policy.closed_content_boundary: This pack does not reproduce complete commercial rulebooks, adventure text, setting chapters, proprietary stat blocks, or closed spell descriptions.
